subject.title: Gateway should expose HTTP REST endpoints for common queries

question: Should the default-off admin HTTP RPC plugin expose read-only session query methods such as `sessions.list` and `sessions.get`/`sessions.describe` for trusted HTTP callers, or should session-data access wait for a separate REST session API design?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but the permanent HTTP exposure boundary for session state and the public API shape are security/product decisions that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Extend admin HTTP RPC
options.body: Add only maintainer-approved read-only session query methods to the existing default-off trusted admin HTTP RPC allowlist with docs and route/allowlist tests.

options.title: Use broader session API tracker
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20934 own the HTTP session API shape and keep this issue as linked context for read-only query needs.

options.title: Keep sessions WebSocket-only
options.body: Document that integrations needing session list/detail state must use Gateway WebSocket RPC and leave HTTP limited to the current admin allowlist.

recommendation.title: Extend admin HTTP RPC
recommendation.body: Add only maintainer-approved read-only session query methods to the existing default-off trusted admin HTTP RPC allowlist with docs and route/allowlist tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The admin HTTP RPC plugin and trusted-operator HTTP boundary history point to steipete as the clearest decision owner.
